issues.evidence: Both editions use reference [43] for the estimate that 29.6% of employed people in 2025-Q3 had some generative-AI exposure and that about 5.2 million were in the highest exposure gradient. The cited URL https://blogdoibre.fgv.br/node/2289 resolves to an unrelated 2023 post about the US banking crisis. The intended primary FGV IBRE article is Daniel Duque, “Inteligência artificial generativa e mercado de trabalho no Brasil: evidências iniciais sobre ocupação e renda”, 27 April 2026, at https://blogdoibre.fgv.br/posts/inteligencia-artificial-generativa-e-mercado-de-trabalho-no-brasil-evidencias-iniciais-sobre; that page contains the 29.6% and 5.2 million figures. The current bibliography therefore fails to provide a source that supports the adjacent claim.
issues.required_correction: Replace reference [43] in both editions with the correct FGV IBRE article URL. Preserve the author, title and 27 April 2026 date; re-open the final URL and confirm that it supports the 29.6% and 5.2 million figures. Keep potential occupational exposure distinct from observed AI adoption and realized employment effects.

issues.evidence: The report describes NBER Working Paper 35275 as a 2026 study and relies on its estimates for more than 500,000 GitHub developers, including cumulative changes in commits, projects and releases. The NBER source page identifies it as Working Paper 35275 (issued May 2026, revised September 2026) and discloses that Mert Demirer and Leon Musolff are paid research consultants to Microsoft. Neither staged edition states that this is a working paper or surfaces the authors' disclosed paid consulting relationships. This relationship does not invalidate the findings, but it is material source context for an independent report using GitHub activity and AI-usage telemetry.
issues.required_correction: In both editions, identify the source as NBER Working Paper 35275, issued May 2026 and revised September 2026, and state that it is a working paper rather than a peer-reviewed journal article. Add a concise, neutral disclosure that the NBER page lists Demirer and Musolff as paid research consultants to Microsoft. Do not infer misconduct or discard the estimates; retain the matched-event-study design, outcome definitions and limits.

issues.evidence: The BLS Graphic Designers Occupational Outlook Handbook page reports a 2% projected decline and explicitly says that the percentage is rounded to the nearest whole number. The detailed BLS occupational projections table reports -1.7% for graphic designers. The charts display -2.0 while the other series use one decimal, implying precision not supplied by the cited rounded source.
issues.required_correction: Use -1.7 in both charts if drawing from the detailed occupational projections table, or use -2 without a decimal if drawing from the rounded Occupational Outlook Handbook page. Keep the source and displayed precision consistent.

issues.evidence: The English title says that AI arrived before the labour market could adjust. The Portuguese title, “A IA chegou antes da transição do trabalho”, shifts the proposition to a transition of work and omits the labour-market adjustment mechanism.
issues.required_correction: Use a semantically equivalent PT-BR title, for example “A IA chegou antes que o mercado de trabalho pudesse se ajustar”, in the pending metadata and staged Markdown.
